title: Completed extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Assume in addition that $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_T$ and $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Identify $A_X|_U=A_U$ and $A_{X'}|_{U'}=A_{U'}$ under the slice-site identifications [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Extension by zero $j_!$ and $j'_!$ means sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf on these ringed slice sites [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], applied termwise to complexes. Let $K\in D(U_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Then $j_!K$ is derived $I$-complete, and the canonical completed base-change map
$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K$, where completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Both sides belong to the derived $I$-complete subcategory of $D(X'_{\Proet},A)$. The canonical map is the one induced by the finite-coefficient extension-by-zero base-change maps and the comparison between extension by zero and the derived limit of the strict reduction tower.

proof.text: For $T=X,X',U,U'$ put $P_n=A/I^n$ and use the completed sheaf $A_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For each pair $(T,W)=(X,U),(X',U')$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $W$'s pro-etale site with the slice site and carries each constant $(P_n)_T$ to $(P_n)_W$. The sectionwise formula for limits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] therefore identifies $A_T|_W$ with $A_W$: on an object $V\to W$ both are the compatible families of sections of $(P_n)_T(V)$. The componentwise identity preserves every projection and quotient map. Since the square is cartesian and $j$ is quasi-compact, [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] makes $j'$ quasi-compact too; there is no quasi-compactness requirement on $g$.

source.place: Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero), slice interpretation; schemes.tex Tag 01K5 (quasi-compact base change).

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to these ringed slice sites. Restriction and sheafified extension by zero are exact, and extension is left adjoint to restriction. Thus [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] supplies their termwise functors on unbounded derived categories. We will also use extension with coefficients $(P_n)_T$; it is the same finite-coefficient functor as [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Extension commutes with restriction of scalars along $A_T\to(P_n)_T$ and along $P_b\to P_a$. Indeed [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] uses the same direct-sum presheaf of abelian groups before and after scalar restriction, with action composed with the ring map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] equips the same abelian sheafification with the unique extending action. The resulting comparison is identity on the underlying abelian sheaf and is natural in every module map. No completed coefficient sheaf is identified with the constant sheaf $A$.

Let $e:W\hookrightarrow T$ be either $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ or $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$, and let $C$ be any complex on $W$. Choose a K-flat representative $P\to C$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The module tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] extends to total tensor complexes: $e_!$ commutes with the direct sums in the totalization because it is a left adjoint [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], and the comparison commutes with the differentials in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For any acyclic $A_T$-complex $N$, restriction $e^*N$ is acyclic by Step 2, so
$$ (e_!P)\otimes_{A_T}N\cong e_!(P\otimes_{A_W}e^*N) $$
is acyclic. Thus $e_!P$ is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Its terms are flat too: for each $q$ the same tensor comparison expresses $(-)\otimes e_!P^q$ as restriction, tensor with the flat $P^q$, and exact extension, which is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Since extension is exact, $e_!P\to e_!C$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The reduction of $e_!C$ is consequently computed by $(e_!P)\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, and the tensor comparison identifies this with $e_!(P\otimes_{A_W}(P_n)_W)$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] these identify the strict reduction towers
$$ (e_!C)_\bullet\cong e_!(C_\bullet). $$
At the presheaf tensor level the comparison sends a generator $s\otimes u$ in the unique summand indexed by a factorization $V\to W$ to the same tensor $s\otimes u$. Applying $q_{b,a}$ on either side sends it to $s\otimes q_{b,a}(u)$, so the comparisons commute with the actual tower maps, not just with their evaluations. Step 2 supplies the scalar-restriction identification on each level. The construction is natural on K-flat representatives and hence in $C$.

proof.text:
Here is the product argument needed in the imported proof (Stacks Tag 09BP), using existing nodes rather than introducing a product lemma. Let $e:W\hookrightarrow T$ be either $j$ or $j'$, let $R=A_T$, and let $(F_s)_{s\in S}$ be a small family of $R|_W$-module sheaves. Choose a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with image $T\setminus W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]. For any $R|_W$-module sheaf $F$, put $H=e_*F$. One has $e^{-1}H=F$: on $V\to W$ the direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] evaluates $H$ as $F(V\times_TW)=F(V)$, under the slice identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Since $e$ is quasi-compact, the exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied to $H$, identifies
$$ e_!F=\ker\big(e_*F\longrightarrow i_*i^{-1}e_*F\big). $$
Both direct images preserve products by the same sectionwise direct-image formula and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. Closed inverse image $i^{-1}$ preserves small limits, including products, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], with target coefficient $i^{-1}R$ (no unrelated scalar extension). Therefore the kernel for $F=\prod_sF_s$ is the product of the kernels for $F_s$: on each section both consist of tuples whose every component maps to zero. Under these identifications the map is precisely the comparison induced by the projections. Hence $e_!(\prod_sF_s)\to\prod_se_!F_s$ is an isomorphism, natural in the family. This is a kernel computation from the cited statements, not an assertion that extension is sectionwise zero on arbitrary test schemes. It includes the empty family.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), kernel proof, using Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion). The stated ringed recollement and module limit nodes supply its module version.

proof.text:
Countable products of module sheaves over each of $A_T,A_W$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core], their termwise product complexes represent products in the unbounded derived categories. Applying the comparison in Step 4 in every cochain degree therefore proves preservation of these derived products by $e_!$. For a countable family of towers $(M_{s,n})_n$, define the tower with level $n$ equal to $\prod_s M_{s,n}$ and transition the unique map whose $s$-th projection is the $s$-th transition followed by projection. A map into it is exactly a family of compatible maps into the given towers, by the product universal property at every level. Hence countable products of towers exist and are computed levelwise. Kernels, cokernels and exactness are levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; exactness of countable products of module sheaves therefore gives exact countable products of towers. The cited derived-product theorem applies also to these tower categories, and the degreewise, levelwise projection comparisons of Step 4 show that extension preserves their countable derived products. Termwise extension commutes with evaluation, and Step 2 made it triangulated. All hypotheses of [lem-cbc-exact-functor-rlim] are now verified. Construct the comparison independently of that theorem using an explicit functorial complex. For a strict tower complex $M_\bullet$, put $P(M)=\prod_nM_n$, $f_M=1-s$, and
$$ H(M)^q=P(M)^q\oplus P(M)^{q-1},\qquad d(x,y)=(dx,f_Mx-dy). $$
A strict tower map $h$ gives $H(h)(x,y)=((\prod_nh_n)x,(\prod_nh_n)y)$. Exact countable products imply that a levelwise quasi-isomorphism induces a quasi-isomorphism on $P$ and hence on $H$, by its mapping-cone triangle. A strict tower chain homotopy $h$ induces the homotopy $(x,y)\mapsto(hx,-hy)$ on $H$: the cross terms cancel because $f h=h f$. Thus $H$ defines a functor on the derived strict-tower category. Choose the functorial K-injective resolution $u_M:M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. The canonical quasi-isomorphism of [lem-weil-derived-limit-roos-complex], after the change of cone coordinates $(y,x)\mapsto(x,-y)$, is
$$ a_I:\lim I_\bullet\longrightarrow H(I_\bullet),\qquad x\longmapsto(\iota x,0). $$
Its hypotheses hold: the module category is Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] and has exact countable products as above. The displayed formula is natural in strict tower maps, since the kernel inclusion and the product projections are natural. Consequently
$$ \theta_M=(H(u_M))^{-1}a_I:\operatorname{Rlim}M_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}H(M_\bullet) $$
is a natural isomorphism, independent of any choice of cone map in a bare triangulated category. For two functorial resolutions, their comparison to a further resolution gives the same formula after localization: each square commutes by $x\mapsto(\iota x,0)$ and the coordinatewise formula for $H(h)$. This identifies $H$ with the specified derived-limit functor, rather than merely choosing an object isomorphic to a derived limit.

Step 4 gives a natural chain isomorphism
$$ \kappa_M:e_!H(M_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(e_!M_\bullet). $$
It is the product comparison on both summands. For the $n$-th coordinate its compatibility with $f_M$ reads $e_!(x_n-t_nx_{n+1})=e_!x_n-e_!t_n(e_!x_{n+1})$; additivity and naturality of the product comparison give this equality. Define
$$ \lambda_e=\theta_{e_!M}^{-1}\,\kappa_M\,e_!(\theta_M):e_!\operatorname{Rlim}M_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Rlim}(e_!M_\bullet). $$
All three maps are natural isomorphisms. This is the resolution/ordinary-limit comparison: for a target resolution $v:e_!I_\bullet\to J_\bullet$, the square from $e_!\lim I_\bullet\cong\lim(e_!I_\bullet)$ to $\lim J_\bullet$ and from $e_!H(I_\bullet)$ to $H(J_\bullet)$ commutes, since both composites send a compatible family $x$ to $( (v_nx_n)_n,0)$. This verifies the identification with the comparison induced by ordinary-limit projections. In the Roos triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], use these fiber presentations: projection to the first summand and the shifted second-product inclusion are the structure maps. The map $\kappa_M$ is the product comparison on each summand, so it commutes with both structure maps and gives precisely $p'\lambda_e=\phi e_!(p)$ and $\lambda_e[1]\xi e_!(\delta)=\delta'\phi$. Thus the current [lem-cbc-exact-functor-rlim] also verifies invertibility of this independently specified comparison; it is not being used to select a canonical comparison.

proof.text: Extension by zero also preserves intrinsic derived completeness. In [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], the Koszul complex $Q_m(A_T)$ is a bounded finite free complex. Its restriction is $Q_m(A_W)$ with the same differential multiplications $a_j^m$ and transition multiplications $a_j$. The tensor comparison of Step 3, or its finite-sum version, identifies $e_!(C\otimes Q_m(A_W))$ with $(e_!C)\otimes Q_m(A_T)$. Step 4 identifies their termwise countable products. Since $e_!$ is additive, it identifies the operator $(z_m)\mapsto(z_m-t_mz_{m+1})$ and the two finite summands and differential of the explicitly defined completion fiber $F(C)$. Moreover, both completion units send $c$ to $((c\otimes1)_m,0)$, so $e_!\eta_C$ is identified with $\eta_{e_!C}$. Consequently $C$ complete implies $e_!C$ complete. Apply this first to $j$ and the given $K$, making $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K$ well-typed. By [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction], $L=Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K$ is complete; apply the same argument to $j'$ and $L$. That lemma applied to $g$ and $j_!K$ also gives completeness of the left-hand side. Thus the displayed comparison will be a map between complete objects.

source.place: Tag 09BP combined with the Koszul completion model; algebraization.tex Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul). The chain-level units are the specified units of the cited intrinsic definition.

proof.text:
Each $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite by the coefficient datum. Finite-coefficient pullback is exact and is the abelian inverse image with action transported through the canonical constant-ring isomorphism [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Thus [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] gives, termwise and naturally,
$$ \beta_n:g_n^*j_!K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n. $$
These maps commute with the quotient transitions, as follows without imposing extra coefficient hypotheses on that lemma. The inverse comparison is the adjoint, under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$, of
$$ g_U^{-1}F\longrightarrow g_U^{-1}j^{-1}j_!F\cong j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F, $$
where the first map is inverse image of the extension/restriction unit, and the second is the composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] for $jg_U=gj'$. The finite base-change map is the inverse of this canonical comparison. The unit at an object factoring through $U$ sends a section to its own extension summand [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]; the adjunction is that of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The inverse-image construction and its unit/counit act on the underlying abelian sheaves as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. All these maps are unchanged when an action is composed with $P_b\to P_a$: scalar restriction does not change the underlying sections, summands or abelian sheafification (Step 2). The composition comparison is characterized by these same adjunctions. It too commutes with scalar restriction. Thus the inverse comparisons commute with every quotient transition, and so do their inverses $\beta_n$. This also shows that applying a chain map or a quotient map before or after $\beta_n$ gives the same underlying map. Combined with Step 3, these are a morphism of the actual strict reduction-tower models, with a levelwise inverse. In passing from completed-coefficient pullback to these finite models use the natural finite-reduction identifications in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The latter explicitly says these identifications commute with the finite quotient transitions; on K-flat tensors they rebracket $(x\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes bc$, and quotient maps replace $b,c$ by their images. Hence no identification of unrelated ambient coefficient categories or merely pointwise isomorphism of incoherent towers is being used.

Fix the coefficient and derived-pair normalization when this construction is expressed in another presentation. Write $c_{g,n}:g^{-1}(P_n)_X\to(P_n)_{X'}$ for the canonical constant-section map. The structure map used here is exactly the $c_g$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], characterized by
$$ \pi_n c_g=c_{g,n}\,g^{-1}(\pi_n). $$
Naturality of the constant-section maps gives
$$ q'_{b,a}c_{g,b}=c_{g,a}\,g^{-1}(q_{b,a}), $$
and hence compatibility for every quotient arrow, including composites and identities. Two proposed completed coefficient maps satisfying these equations are equal by the limit universal property. After this equality, the module pullbacks have the canonical tensor comparison $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes b$; both module-map formulas send it to $g^{-1}(h)(x)\otimes b$, so this is a natural comparison, not merely objectwise identifications. For two left-derived presentations of this same module functor, [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] supplies the universal pair. Its universal property fixes the derived comparison $e$ by
$$ \varepsilon'_P e_{QP}=Q(\alpha_P)\varepsilon_P $$
on every K-flat representative, where $\alpha_P$ is the termwise module comparison. Applying the universal property in both directions makes these comparisons inverse. The same argument levelwise for strict K-flat towers retains the transition maps by the displayed naturality, so it compares the actual derived tower functors with their counits. These assertions compare two constructions of the specified pullback; they do not assume that $c_g$ is invertible or identify unrelated coefficient categories.

proof.text:
Now apply the functorial derived inverse limit [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] to the strict tower comparison of Step 7. By the definition of completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and Step 3, its source is $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K$, and its target is $\operatorname{Rlim}_n(j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n)$. Follow it by $\lambda_{j'}^{-1}$ from Step 5. The result is
$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K
 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Rlim}\beta}\operatorname{Rlim}_n(j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n)
 \xrightarrow{\lambda_{j'}^{-1}}j'_!\operatorname{Rlim}_n(g_{U,n}^*K_n)
 =j'_!Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K.
$$
Both arrows are isomorphisms: the first is the image of a tower isomorphism, the second was proved in Step 5. This is the canonical completed exchange, since it is induced by the finite canonical exchanges and the specified inverse-limit comparison, exactly as in the statement. Every constituent is natural in $K$ (tensor comparisons, finite exchange and the derived-limit functor); their composition is therefore natural. Step 6 supplies all completeness and domain assertions.

This assembly uses the recorded $c_g$ and the recorded strict derived tower functor, rather than substituting the old public Lean abbreviation for a different composite. Its unit normalization can be read before taking derived limits. The quotient augmentation on a flat-term K-flat $P$ is the strict map with components $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Each quotient transition carries this to $x\otimes1$ at the lower level. The coefficient/tensor comparisons of Step 7 carry these maps to the identical maps and preserve the derived counits. Thus the resulting isomorphism $E_g$ between two presentations of the completed pullback satisfies
$$ E_g\,u_g=u'_g\,e_g, $$
where $u_g,u'_g$ are their specified ordinary-to-completed units and $e_g$ is the counit-normalized ordinary comparison. Indeed the constant-tower comparison identifies their constant diagrams, the quotient augmentation agrees at every level by the formula above, and the natural constant-tower/derived-limit unit in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] identifies the composites. The $\lambda$ of Step 5 respects these augmentations: in its fiber coordinates both send a compatible family to $(x,0)$. The finite maps remain the inverse adjoint mates of Step 7, since the summand-inclusion units, coefficient maps and counits used there were kept. Consequently transporting the open comparison by $E_g^{-1}$ on the source and $j'_!E_{g_U}$ on the target preserves that ordinary adjoint-mate normalization. No extra comparison hypothesis is imposed on $g$ or $K$. This is a mathematical normalization requirement for a later Lean binding; it does not assert definitional equality of the existing Lean functors.
